title: Riso three-plate separation

reference.grammar: three-plate risograph of an isometric drawing on grid stock: yellow, blue, fluorescent pink; plates mis-registered by a few px; each plate grained; marbled top faces; keyline near-black where plates overprint

techniques.name: Isometric extrusion by outline drop
techniques.limits: The drop is a column scan, so a depth past the gap to the object below it paints over that object’s top face. Shapes thinner than 4 px have no interior for the ±2 px probe and get no side faces.
techniques.implementation: Each object is a top-face mask drawn in the plane transform; a column scan drops every boundary pixel whose +x or +y probe is empty by the depth, labelling right or left face, top always winning; later objects overwrite earlier ones.

techniques.name: Three-plate coverage split

params.yellow: top faces + corner wash + marker strokes

gain.note: yellow corner wash at its center

techniques.limits: Keylines past ~8 u close the counters of the letters. The wash is one radial falloff from the lower-left corner; past radius 1.3 it covers the whole sheet and reads as a yellow stock.
techniques.implementation: Face labels become three coverage rasters; each raster is coloured mix(white, ink, coverage) on its own canvas and multiplied onto the stock in plate order.

techniques.name: Per-plate register error
techniques.limits: Past ~8 u a plate leaves its keyline and reads as a second drawing. With all three offsets equal there is no fringe and the print reads as flat digital color.
techniques.implementation: Each plate canvas is drawn translated by its own vector; the keyline sits on all three plates, so the offsets show as coloured fringes on every edge and the overprint of all three is the near-black line.

techniques.name: Per-plate ink grain
techniques.limits: floor + gain above 1 clips fills to full coverage and the edge thinning disappears. stochastic above ~0.7 breaks the keyline into specks. A mottle scale under ~20 u reads as a second grain, not as uneven inking.
techniques.implementation: Before colouring, coverage is multiplied by a blurred copy of itself so fills thin toward their edges, and by a slow perlin mottle; after colouring ART.grain runs mono on the plate and paper pixels are reset to white.

techniques.name: Marbled fill from fbm bands
techniques.limits: core ≥ rim removes the half-tone rim and the veins go hard-edged. Above scale ~100 u a top face holds less than one vein. One octave gives smooth contour lines, not marble.
techniques.implementation: Inside the top faces the pink plate is full except where an fbm field crosses zero: the core of the band is paper, the rim half-coverage, which reads as swirls.

techniques.name: Isometric grid stock

params.diagonals: ±30° through the same lattice, 18.2 u apart along a vertical

techniques.limits: Above alpha ~0.35 the grid competes with the keyline. Under a 14 u pitch the three line families merge into a gray tint.
techniques.implementation: Flat gray fill, then verticals and both diagonal families stroked in the grid ink at 16 % before any plate lands.

pass_order: labels · top / right / left per object, back to front
coverage · three rasters from labels, marble cut into pink, wash and strokes into yellow
grain · edge thinning, mottle, mono noise per plate
plates · multiply in order yellow, blue, pink, each translated by its register error
notes: Measured on ref.png: vertical grid pitch 34 px (31.5 u); diagonal spacing along a vertical 19.6 px; grid pixels 14 % darker than stock; stock (234,234,237) std 12 / 255; yellow (233,230,102); pink face (215,144,189) std 45; blue over pink (98,44,117); keyline (60,30,20).
Pink lands 3 px right and 2 px down of blue; yellow 2 px left and 1 px down; the rebuild gives blue its own +1,−2 u so all three plates move in the motion version.
Words are invented. Seeds 601–603, marble 610, mottle 611.
